To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the problem of feature point recognition can be formulated as a classification task, (2) it can be solved efficiently with simple binary features, and (3) the assumption of conditional independence is a reasonable approximation for the problem at hand.

a) a simple Naive Bayesian classifier can be trained to recognize patches containing keypoints in a single pass over the training set; b) it can do this with no preprocessing and with no need to explicitly detect keypoints; c) it can be implemented in just ten lines of C code; and d) it can scale to hundreds of object classes and thousands of training examples with no significant degradation in performance.
a simple, efficient, Naive Bayesian classifier can perform well for the task of feature point recognition in images containing significant perspective distortions.
